item.title: [News] Roku developer repositories moved from GitHub to GitLab
item.description: Roku has moved its developer repositories from GitHub to GitLab, a strategic shift that repositions its source‑code hosting platform. This change means that any developers or tools that rely on Roku’s public code now need to point to GitLab instead of GitHub.

item.title: [News] GPU-unlock: FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000's cards
item.description: A new kernel module, gpu-unlock, allows users to double the FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000 series GPUs without manual driver patches. This performance boost can significantly accelerate matrix-heavy workloads such as LLM prefill, diffusion, and FlashAttention across a range of GPU models.

item.title: [News] Expanding the Cyber Verification ProgramWe’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program, which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals.
item.description: Anthropic has expanded its Cyber Verification Program to offer tiered access to its most advanced Claude models for security teams, granting reduced safeguards for defensive and red‑team work. This initiative aims to give defenders powerful AI capabilities while still limiting malicious use.

item.title: [News] The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
item.description: Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool competing with Zapier, shut down in August, illustrating how larger platforms like OpenAI, Google, and Apple are consolidating AI features into their own ecosystems. The article highlights a broader trend of AI initiatives being abandoned, with 42% of corporate AI projects ultimately failing to sustain.
